name: sea fairies

attributes.attribute: lived on ocean islands and in the waves
home of the Fairies beyond hills and bogs

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Sea fairies, called na buchtogai in Irish, were creatures of the Otherworld. The Fairies did not live only beneath hills and in deep bogs. They also lived on islands in the sea, especially islands that vanish behind mist. Some lived in the ocean waves. Sea fairies often disguised themselves as seals. Their freshwater kin, the swan maidens, changed into swans instead. Folklore says that marriage between a sea fairy and a human was common. Many coastal families claimed seal ancestry from such a match.
objective: Document the sea fairies of Scottish and Irish folklore.
key_results: Record the Irish name na buchtogai for sea fairies.
Record their homes on misty islands and in the waves.
Record their habit of disguising themselves as seals.
